summary.headline: ABLBL Q2 FY27 revenue rose 11% YoY to INR2,266 crore and EBITDA margin expanded 60 bps to 17.2%, with PAT more than doubling to INR53 crore.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 11% YoY to INR2,266 crore, led by Lifestyle Brands (+9%, INR1,906 crore) and Emerging Brands (+27%, INR371 crore). EBITDA rose 15% to INR390 crore with margin up 60 bps to 17.2%, and PAT grew 126% to INR53 crore. Retail like-to-like growth was 5.3% in Q2 but September LFL was zero due to the festive-calendar shift, while the company added over 100 stores, its highest quarterly addition in more than 2 years. Management guided to continued double-digit growth in steady state, a net debt target of about INR600 crore by Q4, and capex of about INR300 crore on track.

financial_highlights.change: Down vs same period last year

segments.name: Lifestyle Brands
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,906 crore (+9% YoY), EBITDA INR371 crore (+10%), margin 19.5%. Retail LFL 5.3% in Q2 and 6.6% in H1; September LFL was zero due to festive shift.

segments.name: Emerging Brands (Reebok, Van Heusen Innerwear, American Eagle)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR371 crore (+27%), like-to-like growth 11%, EBITDA margin 6.8% (+530 bps). Reebok opened its 250th India store; management expects over 300 Reebok stores by year-end.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail revenue +8% YoY with LFL 5.3% across 3,000+ stores; small-town network (500+ stores) has delivered double-digit LFL for six consecutive quarters. Network at 3,434 stores across 800+ cities, about 5.1 million sq ft.

segments.name: Wholesale and e-commerce
segments.commentary: Wholesale grew 18% and e-commerce 12% YoY. Management said e-commerce secondary sales were healthy double-digit through H1.

guidance_outlook: Management expects steady-state double-digit growth; aspiration remains around 15% but management earlier guided 11-12% revenue and slightly better EBITDA growth.
Like-to-like growth steady state of 7-8%, per management.
Net debt target close to INR600 crore by Q4 FY27 from about INR950 crore currently; management said broadly on track.
Capex for FY27 about INR300 crore, more or less on track.
Price increases of about 6% taken for the season, with the full effect expected in Q3; a small part reflected in Q2.
Management expects one profitable quarter for Innerwear this year.
Festive season started encouragingly; management expects an even stronger H2. H2 store closures expected to be lower than H1 (about 90 net closures in H1 from about 180 gross additions).
capex_capacity: Over 100 stores added in Q2, highest quarterly addition in more than 2 years; management aims to sustain this pace and expects Q3 and beyond expansion to be stronger.
Retail network 3,434 stores across more than 800 cities and towns, about 5.1 million sq ft.
Reebok: 250+ exclusive stores; target above 300 by year-end; typical store 1,000-1,100 sq ft.
H1 gross store additions about 180 with net addition about 90 (closures about 90-100).
Capex guidance about INR300 crore for FY27, on track.
demand_pricing: Like-to-like Q2 5.3%, H1 6.6%; September LFL zero due to festive shift, which management said would have been about 8%+ otherwise.
Small towns: about 2,500 towns (population below about 1.5 lakh), about 500+ stores, about half Peter England; they contribute about 5-6% of sales.
Casual vs formal mix about 51:49 or 49:51 per management; Q3 expected to be more wedding-heavy.
VYBE collection contributes about 10% of sales in stores carrying it and brought about 50,000 new consumers in their 20s.
Price increase about 6% against cost inflation; management says vendor partners absorbed part of cost increases.
Pre-Ind AS margin not reported quarterly; management says it improved and will be shared once a year.

qa_highlights.question: Will double-digit growth continue into Q3 and can growth move closer to 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said double-digit is expected in steady state, with expansion stronger in Q3 and beyond; it declined to commit to 15% and said aspirations remain higher than 11-12%.

qa_highlights.question: What price increases and inflation are in the portfolio?
qa_highlights.answer: About 6% price increase taken for the season, with the full effect in Q3; a small part is in Q2 with a mix of old and new inventory, and vendor partners absorbed part of costs.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt targets and net cash positive goal?
qa_highlights.answer: Target close to INR600 crore net debt by Q4; currently about INR930-950 crore, and H2 cash flows are stronger.

qa_highlights.question: Why no operating leverage on a pre-Ind AS basis (analyst-computed H1 margin about 6.1% vs 6.4%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the analyst's calculation is not the correct method for pre-Ind AS margin due to store openings and closures; margins improved at all levels and MIS EBITDA grew a couple of points faster than sales, with advertising investment.

qa_highlights.question: Emerging brands margin drivers and targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers are operating leverage, discount reduction, store-level leverage at double-digit LFL, and lower store costs; Reebok should eventually match other brands' margins less royalty.

qa_highlights.question: E-commerce slowed to 12% growth; what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: E-commerce mixes marketplace and B2B; secondary sales were healthy double-digit through H1. Q3 growth expected to stay around H1 levels, not Q1 levels.

qa_highlights.question: When will Innerwear break even?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Innerwear India EBITDA margin of 6.5-6.8% vs 1.5% a year ago and said it expects one profitable quarter this year.

risks_watch: Price increase of about 6% may face consumer pushback and lead to higher discounting.
Raw material and vendor cost inflation, with the bigger impact expected in H2.
Pre-Ind AS margin disclosure is annual only, so analysts cannot verify lease-adjusted margin trend quarterly; questions remained open.
Like-to-like was zero in September; festive timing may distort Q3 comparisons.
Net debt reduction to about INR600 crore by Q4 depends on H2 cash flows.
Management did not commit to 15% growth; current guidance is 11-12% revenue growth.
summary.management_tone: Confident on brand and store momentum and on Emerging Brands margin, but guarded on the 15% growth ambition and evasive on pre-Ind AS margins and lifestyle-only store counts, which were deferred to offline follow-up.
key_quotes: Importantly, this marks our 4th consecutive quarter of double-digit revenue growth and 5th consecutive quarter of margin expansion.

Our holy grail, Abhijeet, is always going to be built around how do we keep driving greater throughputs from our retail stores.
Margin has expanded, so you'll have to help me understand where you got that. We've actually expanded margin.
We're pushing ourselves very hard to be able to deliver that.

adds.what: Over 100 Retail stores added in Q2 FY27 (highest quarterly addition in 2+ years); network at 3,434 stores, ~5.1 mn sq ft
Reebok exclusive stores: 250th store opened, target above 300 by year-end FY27 (typical 1,000-1,100 sq ft)

growth.why: Management guides to steady-state double-digit growth (aspiration ~15%, earlier 11-12% revenue guidance), backed by 100+ store adds in Q2, Reebok 300+ store target by year-end, ~6% price increases with full effect in Q3, and H1 gross store additions of ~180; capex of ~INR300 crore for FY27 is on track, but no specific order or capacity-to-revenue quantification was given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin rose 60 bps to 17.2% and H1 by 50 bps to 16.6%; Emerging Brands margin up 530 bps to 6.8% on operating leverage and discount reduction, and ~6% price increase has full effect in Q3 with vendors absorbing part of cost inflation, though raw material inflation is expected to hit more in H2.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Over 100 stores added in Q2 (highest in 2+ years), H1 gross additions ~180 with net ~90, management expects Q3 and beyond expansion to be stronger, and Reebok targets 300+ stores by year-end from 250 today.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Retail LFL 5.3% in Q2 and 6.6% in H1 with steady-state LFL of 7-8%, plus wholesale +18%, e-commerce +12%, and Q3 expected to be more wedding-heavy; ~6% price increase means part of growth is price.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No new capex program or capacity announcement discussed; the existing ~INR300 crore FY27 capex is on track, and utilisation was not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to commit to 15% growth and kept revenue guidance at 11-12%, with steady-state double-digit growth only; Q2 revenue +11% and H1 +11% sit within that range.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: September LFL was zero due to festive shift, price increases may cause discounting, and raw material and vendor inflation is expected to bite more in H2, while net debt target depends on H2 cash flows.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No specific new product or brand launch was discussed beyond VYBE collection's existing ~10% share of sales in stores carrying it.

rows.label: Net debt to ~INR600 crore by Q4 FY27
rows.why: Net debt was about INR950 crore (INR956 crore in Q2) and management said it is broadly on track to reach close to INR600 crore, with stronger H2 cash flows, though this depends on those flows.

rows.label: Innerwear profitable quarter this year
rows.why: Innerwear India EBITDA margin rose to 6.5-6.8% from 1.5% a year ago and management expects one profitable quarter this year.

rows.label: Small-town network LFL momentum
rows.why: Small-town network of 500+ stores has delivered double-digit LFL for six consecutive quarters and contributes about 5-6% of sales, supporting volume.

tone.note: Management was confident on store and brand momentum, Emerging Brands margins and deleveraging, but guarded on the 15% growth aspiration and evasive on pre-Ind AS margins, which were deferred to offline follow-up; analysts pushed on operating leverage, pre-Ind AS margin and e-commerce slowdown.
